edges.description: Inoculated spirochetes acquire host proteolytic activity that supports invasion and dissemination.
Disseminated spirochetes produce high-density bacteremia and the antigenic variants that drive recurrent waves.
Bloodstream spirochetes interact with red cells and contribute to macrophage clearance in liver and spleen.
Each bacteremic serotype elicits a rapid IgM response that clears that wave.
Uncontrolled high-density bacteremia can progress to severe systemic complications.
Bacteremic febrile waves are accompanied by chills and rigors.
The systemic bacteremic illness commonly includes arthralgia.
The systemic bacteremic illness can produce a rash.
High-density spirochetemia in pregnancy precipitates birth during the febrile attack.
Serotype clearance leaves rare Vmp switch variants to seed the next bacteremic relapse.
Tissue macrophage removal of erythrocytes contributes to anemia.
Platelet counts fall during the high-level relapsing-fever bacteremia.
Bacteremic waves drive recurrent febrile episodes.
Severe disease can progress to acute respiratory distress syndrome.
Severe disease can produce shock and hypotension.
Severe systemic disease can produce altered mental status.
The transient cytokine surge manifests clinically as the Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction.
The mouse model reproduces the thrombocytopenia and anemia of relapsing fever.
edges.limitations: Inbred strains differ in innate susceptibility, and mice are not the natural human host.

nodes.description: The first antibiotic dose lyses the high-density spirochetemia and precipitates a Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction: an iatrogenic surge of TNF-alpha, IL-6, and IL-8 with rigors, fever, and hypotension, distinct from the burden-driven progression of untreated disease.

evidence.reference_title: Detection of plasma tumor necrosis factor, interleukins 6, and 8 during the Jarisch-Herxheimer Reaction of relapsing fever.
evidence.snippet: a seven-, six-, and fourfold elevation of these plasma cytokine concentrations over admission levels was detected, respectively, occurring in transient form coincidental with observed pathophysiological changes of J-HR.

evidence.reference_title: Prevention of Jarisch-Herxheimer reactions by treatment with antibodies against tumor necrosis factor alpha.
evidence.snippet: Ten of the 20 patients given anti-TNF-alpha Fab had Jarisch-Herxheimer reactions with rigors, as compared with 26 of the 29 control patients (P = 0.006).

nodes.description: Arthralgia is a common symptom of relapsing fever.

evidence.reference_title: Characteristics of Hard Tick Relapsing Fever Caused by Borrelia miyamotoi, United States, 2013-2019.
evidence.snippet: Fever and headache were common symptoms; 28% of case-patients reported recurring fevers, 55% had arthralgia, and 16% had a rash.

nodes.description: Lice, Ornithodoros soft ticks, and Ixodes hard ticks deliver relapsing-fever Borrelia from the vector cycle into a mammalian host.

evidence.reference_title: Inactivation of genes for antigenic variation in the relapsing fever spirochete Borrelia hermsii reduces infectivity in mice and transmission by ticks.
evidence.snippet: The mutant lacking Vtp also colonized ticks but produced neither Vtp nor a Vmp in tick salivary glands, which rendered the spirochete noninfectious by tick bite.

nodes.description: Peromyscus reservoir rodents carry relapsing-fever Borrelia with partial resistance and infection tolerance, so they do not reproduce the severe human disease.

Relapsing-fever Borrelia bind host plasminogen and generate surface plasmin, giving the spirochete host proteolytic activity that degrades fibrin and extracellular matrix and facilitates bloodstream and tissue dissemination.

evidence.reference_title: Interaction of spirochetes with the host fibrinolytic system and potential roles in pathogenesis.
evidence.snippet: Spirochetes equipped with Pla activity have been shown to degrade extracellular matrix (ECM) components, in addition to digesting fibrin, facilitating bacterial invasion and dissemination.

evidence.snippet: Risk of birth during the attack of TBRF was 58.0%, with an extremely high perinatal mortality of 436 per 1000 births.

nodes.description: Rare variants switch silent variable major protein cassettes into the single expression site, changing the dominant surface antigen after an antibody response clears the previous serotype and restarting bacteremia.

evidence.reference_title: Cis-acting DNA elements flanking the variable major protein expression site of Borrelia hermsii are required for murine persistence.
evidence.snippet: In Borrelia hermsii, antigenic variation occurs as a result of a nonreciprocal gene conversion event that places one of ~60 silent variable major protein genes downstream of a single, transcriptionally active promoter.

evidence.snippet: spirochetes repeatedly evade the host's acquired immune response by undergoing antigenic variation of the variable major proteins (Vmps) produced on their outer surface.
